headings: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.

units.short_original_anchor: Of a Thief and Theft.
units.normalized_historical_statement: This heading begins the requested theft material on printed page 330.

units.short_original_anchor: Haly saith, you must know that the ascendant is the Signifi-
units.normalized_historical_statement: The passage attributes to Haly the assignment of the ascendant as significator of the querent.
preconditions: A question concerning theft or something taken away.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The anchor retains the printed line-ending division of Significator.

units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the second is Significator of the
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the method attributed to Haly, the lord of the second signifies the thing stolen or taken away.
preconditions: A question concerning theft or something taken away.

units.short_original_anchor: and the seventh house is the Significator of the Thiefe
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the method attributed to Haly, the seventh house signifies the thief if there is no peregrine planet in an angle or second house.
preconditions: No peregrine planet is in an angle or second house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The following paragraph supplies an alternative priority for a peregrine planet.

units.short_original_anchor: the tenth house is the Signifier of the
units.normalized_historical_statement: The tenth house signifies the king. The sentence continues across the page boundary: the sign of the fourth signifies the place where the thing is, or from which it was taken away.
preconditions: The theft method attributed to Haly.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The original errata leaf has an entry for printed page 330, line 6, directing the reading 'of'; the visible body text already reads 'of the' here.
The bottom catchword 'King,' repeats the opening word on printed page 331.

units.short_original_anchor: you must know from the Lords of those houses
units.normalized_historical_statement: The reader is directed to learn the proper significations from the lords of the assigned houses, thereby judging the condition and state of what is missing.
preconditions: The preceding assignments of houses and significators.

units.short_original_anchor: if you find in the ascendant a Planet peregrine
units.normalized_historical_statement: A peregrine planet in the ascendant is to be taken as significator of the thief, especially if it is lord of the seventh house.
preconditions: A peregrine planet is in the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Being lord of the seventh strengthens this assignment; it is not stated as necessary.

units.short_original_anchor: but if no Planet be in the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: If there is no planet in the ascendant, inspect the other angles and assign a planet found there as significator of the thief.
preconditions: No planet is in the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This clause does not explicitly repeat the peregrine qualification.

units.short_original_anchor: This shall be more copiously handled in some Chapters following.
units.normalized_historical_statement: A marginal note promises fuller treatment in following chapters and calls the present method 'A most certain rule.'
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is the historical author's assessment of the rule.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.normalized_historical_statement: A separate subsection addresses selection of the thief's significator.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh commonly signifies the Thief
units.normalized_historical_statement: The lord of the seventh commonly signifies the thief, especially when peregrine in the ascendant or another angle.
preconditions: A theft question.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Peregrinity and angular placement strengthen the common assignment.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: then behold if any other Planet be pe-
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the seventh does not meet the preceding description, take another peregrine planet in an angle as the thief.
preconditions: The lord of the seventh is not as described in the preceding rule.
Another planet is peregrine in an angle.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed 'if he be not so' refers back to the preceding combined description.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: take the Lord of the hour, and call
units.normalized_historical_statement: If no planet is peregrine in any angle, take the lord of the hour as the thief.
preconditions: No planet is peregrine in any angle.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the fourth be Lord of the seventh
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the fourth is also lord of the seventh and is in the ascendant, the author calls the indication more radical and identifies the querent as the thief. He restricts this rule to cases in which suspicion concerns the querent's fidelity or the querent is most suspected.
preconditions: The lord of the fourth is also lord of the seventh.
That lord is in the ascendant.
Suspicion concerns the querent's fidelity, or the querent is the most suspected person.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This records a historical astrological accusation rule, not evidence of an actual theft.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: whose complexion and condition is ac-
units.normalized_historical_statement: The complexion and condition of the person described in the preceding rule are assigned according to the planet ruling the seventh and its sign.
preconditions: The preceding restricted identification of the querent as thief.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No specific complexion or condition is supplied on these pages.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: A Planet is then peregrin when he is
units.normalized_historical_statement: The marginal definition calls a planet peregrine when it is in none of its own house, triplicity, term, exaltation or face.
preconditions: Determining whether a candidate planet is peregrine.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: I rather and more assured- ly prefer the
units.normalized_historical_statement: A marginal authorial preference favors the lord of the seventh as a more rational and conscientious significator, qualifying the alternative selection methods in the body text.
preconditions: Choosing the thief's significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The anchor preserves the visible division of 'assuredly'.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.normalized_historical_statement: A separate subsection addresses the stolen object's significator.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: The Significator of the thing stolen is the Lord of the Term
units.normalized_historical_statement: The starred rule assigns the stolen object's significator to the lord of the term occupied by the Moon.
preconditions: Determining the significator of the stolen thing.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This differs from the second-house-lord assignment elsewhere in the window.
The adjoining starred marginal note explicitly discounts this rule.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: This rule is vulgar, and not of any cre-
units.normalized_historical_statement: The starred marginal note calls the Moon's term-lord rule vulgar and of no credit.
preconditions: The starred rule assigning the stolen object to the Moon's term lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The criticism belongs specifically to the starred rule.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: the ascendant is Signifier of the question, or Demandant
units.normalized_historical_statement: After finding the thief's significator and understanding its disposition from the significant planet and its aspects, treat the ascendant as significator of the question or demandant.
preconditions: The thief's significator has been found.
Its disposition has been considered through the planet and its aspects.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the ascendant draw towards the Lord
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the ascendant draws toward the lord of the seventh or lord of the hour, or is in the seventh, the author judges that the thief will be taken soon afterward or that recovery of the lost thing is hoped for.
preconditions: The lord of the ascendant draws toward the lord of the seventh, draws toward the lord of the hour, or occupies the seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source offers capture or hope of recovery as alternatives, not guaranteed recovery.

units.short_original_anchor: Of THEFTS.
units.normalized_historical_statement: This heading begins another set of theft rules.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The heading contains fewer than five words.

units.short_original_anchor: The first house, which is the ascendant, is for the querent
units.normalized_historical_statement: The first house, or ascendant, represents the querent, and its lord represents the person who has lost the goods. The sentence continues onto printed page 332.
preconditions: A theft or lost-goods question.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The bottom catchword 'his' repeats the first word on the next page.

units.short_original_anchor: and signifieth the place from whence the Goods was taken
units.normalized_historical_statement: The opening continuation also assigns the place from which the goods were taken to the preceding first-house/first-lord description.
preconditions: The first-house and first-lord assignment continued from printed page 331.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The grammar leaves the precise antecedent of 'signifieth' between the first house and its lord implicit.

units.short_original_anchor: the seventh house and his Lord, and the peregrine Planet
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh house and its lord, the peregrine planet in an angle, and the lord of the hour signify the thief or person who took the goods away.
preconditions: A theft or lost-goods question.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This passage lists the candidates together without an explicit selection order.

units.short_original_anchor: This is a ve- ry good judg- ment, and
units.normalized_historical_statement: The marginal note beside the opening assignments calls this a very good judgment that may well be trusted.
preconditions: The adjoining opening judgment under 'Of THEFTS.'
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The anchor preserves printed word divisions; this is the author's historical endorsement.

units.short_original_anchor: The second house and the Lord of the second house
units.normalized_historical_statement: The second house, its lord and the Moon signify goods or a thing lost, stolen or missing.
preconditions: A theft or lost-goods question.

units.short_original_anchor: the fourth house and his Lord shall signifie the place
units.normalized_historical_statement: The fourth house and its lord signify where the thing has been laid, put, done or conveyed, and where it is at that instant.
preconditions: A theft or lost-goods question.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The body visibly includes the word 'done' in this sequence.

units.short_original_anchor: shall tell and shew whether the Goods shall be found
units.normalized_historical_statement: Whether the goods will be found or recovered is to be judged from the aspects of the Sun and Moon, of the ascendant lord, of the second-house lord, and of the lord of the Moon's house toward the ascendant lord, together with their applications and aspects to one another.
preconditions: Examining the listed planets and house lords, their applications and mutual aspects.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed punctuation does not separately specify a target for every item in the list.

units.short_original_anchor: If the lord of the second and the
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the second-house lord and Moon are in the seventh in the sign of the seventh, and the seventh-house lord beholds them both by trine or sextile, the goods are judged taken away by somebody rather than simply lost. The rule still applies when the aspect is far from exact, described as many degrees distant.
preconditions: The second-house lord and Moon occupy the seventh in its sign.
The seventh-house lord aspects both by trine or sextile.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author expressly allows a distant aspect.

units.short_original_anchor: then hath the party lost the thing or Goods
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the second, is in the house of the lord of the hour, and goes to conjunction with the lord of the seventh, the person is judged to have left the thing somewhere and forgotten it: the goods are carelessly mislaid.
preconditions: The Moon is lady of the second.
The Moon occupies the house of the lord of the hour.
The Moon is going to conjunction with the seventh-house lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source explicitly describes the thing as neither lost nor stolen, but carelessly mislaid.

units.short_original_anchor: the thing is not stolen, but taken away in jest
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the ascendant and occupies the fourth, while the second-house lord is in the seventh or the sign of the eighth house, with the printed conjunction relation 'to the second house' and a sextile or trine to the Moon, the thing is judged taken away in jest.
preconditions: The Moon is lady of the ascendant.
The Moon occupies the fourth.
The second-house lord is in the seventh or in the sign of the eighth house.
The text specifies conjunction 'to the second house'.
The text specifies sextile or trine to the Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The conjunction 'to the second house' is unusual but is preserved without substituting an unstated planet.
The grammatical attachment of the last two aspect clauses is not entirely explicit.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods stolen and taken away
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the ascendant and is in the ascendant, not far removed, and the Sun as lord of the second is in sextile with the lord of the seventh, while the seventh-house lord oppresses the Moon by square, the goods are judged stolen and taken away.
preconditions: The Moon is lady of the ascendant.
The Moon is in the ascendant and 'not farre remote'.
The Sun is lord of the second.
The Sun is in sextile with the seventh-house lord.
The seventh-house lord squares the Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not specify the reference point or numerical distance for 'not farre remote'.

units.short_original_anchor: if the Moon be in the third
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is in the third and oppressed by the seventh-house lord's square, and the second-house lord is also lord of the ascendant and occupies the seventh in the sign of the seventh, the thing is judged stolen.
preconditions: The Moon occupies the third.
The seventh-house lord squares and oppresses the Moon.
The second-house lord also rules the ascendant.
That shared lord occupies the seventh in its sign.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The anchor renders the clearly visible lunar glyph as 'Moon'; the surrounding original words are consecutive.

units.short_original_anchor: but first it was taken in jest
units.normalized_historical_statement: For the preceding third-house-Moon configuration, the author adds that the thing was first taken in jest and will be difficult to recover, except when the Sun and Moon behold the ascendant.
preconditions: The full configuration in A1035.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The Sun and Moon beholding the ascendant are the explicit exception to difficulty recovering the thing.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The original errata leaf reads 'p 330 l 6 r of'. The visible theft paragraph already has 'the Signifier of the' before its terminal 'King,' catchword.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: Records the relevant erratum without introducing a different reading.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The Moon's term lord is assigned to the stolen thing in the starred body rule, but the starred margin calls that rule vulgar and of no credit. Other passages assign the second-house lord, second house and Moon.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: The competing method and its explicit rejection must remain distinct.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The body offers angular peregrine planets and the hour lord as alternatives, while the margin expressly prefers the seventh-house lord.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: Preserves the author's qualification of significator priority.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The 'taken away in jest' paragraph visibly specifies conjunction 'to the second house'; it does not clearly name a planetary target for that conjunction.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: Do not silently repair the unusual relation or infer an omitted planet.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The recovery-method paragraph lists several aspecting bodies and lords, but its punctuation leaves the targets of some listed aspects implicit.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: Avoid assigning directions beyond those stated.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: 'Not farre remote' has no explicit reference point or distance in the visible paragraph.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: No numerical orb or exact proximity criterion can be supplied.

stop_boundary_observed: Began PDF364 immediately below 'Of a Thief and Theft.', excluding the earlier accepted material. Read through PDF365 and PDF366 to the final 'ascendant' sentence and the bottom catchword 'If'. No text from the following page was supplied or inferred. Inspected the original errata leaf for entries relevant to printed pages 330–332; identified the printed-page-330 correction. Handwritten numbering and running titles were not treated as operative source rules.
